text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The agreement on special ties between Bosnia's Serb republic and neighbouring Yugoslavia is a step towards creating a Greater Serbia only this time in peace, diplomats say.
- Local elections in the divided Bosnian town of Mostar have already been held and should not be repeated in the country's local elections, Mostar deputy mayor Safet Orucevic says.
- If 51 percent of Bosnian parliament deputies oppose the draft agreement between the Serb republic and Yugoslavia then it will simply be invalid, German Ambassador to Bosnia Johanes Praisinger says.
- The five-party opposition coalition Joint List calls for the establishment of proper state institutions at all levels instead of a government run by political cliques.
- Moslem deputy mayor of Mostar, Safet Orucevic, says he is ready to allow Bosnian Croats to return to the Moslem controlled east part of the bitterly divided town.
